title: quivive tile data
description: Data for the bundled `quivive` tile: the fleet-presence status bar for one or more repositories that quivive watches. The tile is DATA-DRIVEN — waybar always references `quivive`, and the template renders by what you send: a header driven by the overall `status`, one compact row per entry in `repos[]`, and an attention line per attention item any repo carries. Feed it as `quivive tile --stream`'s stdout (JSON) or, one-shot, `quivive tile`. The contract this schema transcribes lives in the quivive repo (`docs/tile-contract.md`); that page is the source of truth and this file follows it. Unknown fields are tolerated everywhere on purpose: adding a field is an additive change under that contract, and a consumer is required to ignore what it does not know. The five files in `samples/` are byte-identical copies of quivive's `tests/goldens/{all-quiet,active,human-needed,drained,no-fleet}.json` — never hand-edit one side.

v.description: The tile contract version. Moves only on a breaking change — a removed or renamed field, a changed type, a changed meaning, or a changed severity order (S12/S13 of docs/spec.md in the quivive repo).

at.description: RFC 3339, UTC. The clock this tick was computed against — not "now" at read time, and read exactly once for the whole payload, however many repos it covers. This tile's template does not render it (the header renders from `status` alone), but every payload carries it.

status.description: The overall status across every watched repo — one of quivive's five S8 states, in the same precedence order S8 derives per-repo status: human-needed (any repo has an attention item) beats active (any repo has a live agent) beats drained (a plan or recent fleet evidence exists somewhere but nothing is live) beats all-quiet (pact state exists but nothing is moving) beats no-fleet (no pact state anywhere). Nothing in the payload encodes that order — it is the renderer's, and it drives the tile's accent icon/colour and whether it pulses.

repos.description: One entry per repository quivive's tick read this cycle, in registry order. Empty when the registry is empty or missing, which reads as an overall `no-fleet`.

name.description: The repo's directory basename — what a bar has room to print. Two checkouts of the same project share it; `path` is what tells them apart.

path.description: The full, canonicalized path — what a human needs when two checkouts share a `name`. Not rendered by this tile's template today (no row has room for it), but part of the payload and kept in the samples for byte-for-byte fidelity with quivive's goldens.

status.description: This repo's own S8 status (RepoAssessment.status). The payload's overall `status` is the worst of these.

agents.description: Counts over this repo's remembered agents, one bucket per state of the four-state machine (S7: ACTIVE/IDLE/STALE/DEAD). Always all four keys, zeros included. Counts, not a per-agent list — `quivive why` (S21) is where a human goes for names.

idle.description: Agents alive but not currently working.

stale.description: Agents past the stale threshold — quiet, not yet presumed gone. A stale holder never produces a `dead_holding_paths` item.

dead.description: Agents past the dead threshold — presumed gone; any lease one still holds is an attention item.

attention.description: This repo's attention items (RepoAssessment.attention, S16-S18), already sorted and deterministic. Empty is the normal case; any non-empty array is what makes this repo's status `human-needed`.

attentionItem.$comment: Tagged union on `kind` (serde tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case"), mirroring quivive's AttentionItem exactly — see the state seam (src/state.rs) in the quivive repo. FleetDrained (S19) is deliberately absent: it's a transition event for `quivive watch`, not a per-repo attention item. A new `kind` is an additive change, so a renderer must skip one it does not know rather than fail.

agent.description: The dead (or unknown) holder's agent id.

paths.description: That holder's held paths, repo-relative and sorted. One item per holder, not per lease.

remaining_ttl.description: Seconds until pact's sweeper reclaims the most urgent of that holder's leases — the minimum across them, clamped at 0 rather than left negative.

bead_id.description: A bead id filed as needing a decision, from the committed sidecar, verbatim.

started_id.description: The bead/task id that started work in a later wave.

open_gate_id.description: The earliest still-open gate blocking it — only the earliest is reported, so closing gates one at a time does not reshuffle the set.
